articles.content: “It has to be bigger. We have to make it better. We have to deal with all of the financial implications, safety implications, crew implications, everything that goes around that. And it’s a challenge, but we’re all here. We’re all up for it.” “I think it also had to do with the evolution of documentaries … and it felt like now was the time to tell his story the way that we had envisioned.” “I think anytime a power-system structure is proven wrong, it’s an important thing to document.” “Sadly, there is a series that we’ve created called Lost Women , and sadly there are so many voices that need to be restored. And we are happy to do the job.” “He particularly wanted to kind of open himself in a new way for this. He would often say ‘Oh, I want to say this in a new way.’ He wanted to meet me really right where I was.” “[The practice of bottom trawling] is as common as plowing a field… and yet people have never seen images of it before. And so, I think it was a real revelation in the film that this is what industrial fishing really looks like.” “There’s no point in me rehashing what everybody knows, everybody’s seen a thousand times. There’s no significance to that. We want to be able to dig a little bit deeper into the culture, into the culinary culture, but also the culture of the city itself, or the place itself, or the people themselves.” “I think what this documentary allows us to do is to show people that you can be courageously vulnerable. You can care about people’s hearts and you can compete to master your craft.” “…Now I’m making all the things I’ve ever wanted to make, and YouTube has allowed me to do that without needing permission from gatekeepers or a studio.”

articles.title: Jacob Elordi To Star In Adaptation Of ‘The Executioner’s Song’ From United Artists
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Scott Stuber’s United Artists has acquired the rights to the 1982 motion picture The Executioner’s Song and set Oscar nominee Jacob Elordi to produce and star in the pic. Based on Norman Mailer’s landmark 1979 Pulitzer-winning true-life novel, Elordi will play convicted murderer Gary Gilmore. While he has had exec producing credits in the past, this will mark the first time he is a hands on producer in the development process. UA’s Stuber and Nick Nesbitt will produce alongside Elordi, his manager Matt Vioral and producer Sherry Marsh. Filmmaker Lawrence Schiller — who directed the original 1982 film and conducted the extensive interviews with Gilmore, his family and key figures that formed the foundation of Mailer’s book — will serve as an executive producer. Mailer’s masterpiece chronicles the true story of Gilmore, a cold-blooded murderer who, after being tried and convicted for killing two men in Utah, insisted on being executed for his crimes. Fighting attorneys for a legal system intent on keeping him alive long after it sentenced him to death, Gilmore became a national media sensation and the first person executed in the United States following a four-year de facto moratorium on capital punishment. Told with impressive authority and compassion, The Executioner’s Song journeys deep into the heart of American violence, media frenzy and loneliness. He gained widespread acclaim for his work in the award-winning series Euphoria and the World War II limited series The Narrow Road to the Deep North , which earned him an AACTA Award for Best Lead Actor in a Drama. articles.title: Daisy Ridley, Darren Criss, Travis Fimmel & Judy Greer Join Catherine Zeta-Jones In Tate Taylor’s Marriage Counselor Thriller ‘Cupid
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE : Here’s some nice casting. Daisy Ridley ( Ebenezer ), Darren Criss ( Glee ), Travis Fimmel ( Dune: Prophecy ) and Judy Greer ( Ant-Man ) have joined Catherine Zeta-Jones in Tate Taylor’s psychological thriller Cupid , which is now filming in Natchez, Mississippi. Tate Taylor ( The Girl On The Train ) is directing from a screenplay by the Van Dyke brothers ( Don’t Worry Darling ). Cupid “follows a couple (Ridley and Criss) whose relationship is on the rocks as they try, over one weekend, to repair their marriage at the home of a seemingly helpful but unorthodox marriage counselor (Zeta-Jones). What starts out as a hopeful endeavor quickly turns dark as her methods become crueler and more dangerous.” Taylor and John Norris are producing alongside Ryan Donnell Smith. Executive producers include Brian Edwards, Zack Sherman, Jon Hamm and Jaan Bains for Time Zone Capital. This leads them to travel to Mexico out of spite, where they try showing each other up with new dates. Watch on Deadline The pic is based on a spec by David Bernstein. Brown and Jake Bongiovi will produce for PCMA ( Damsel , Enola Holmes ), alongside Andrew Swett and Aaron Ryder for Embrace Entertainment (Netflix’s Office Romance ) and Will Speck and Josh Gordon for Speck + Gordon Inc. Executive producers are Brown for PCMA, Eric Fineman and David Kern. Execs were on the lookout for fresh takes and knew they’d found the one in new writer Bernstein’s spec when the team started quoting its one-liners and referencing its set pieces around the office. At Netflix, Brown has become synonymous with hit genre fare like Stranger Things , Damsel and the Enola Holmes films. Swiss filmmaker Gabriel Tejedor directed the feature documentary that explores “the contradictions of a Bulgarian town pulled into Europe’s shifting geopolitical order, where arms production for Ukraine’s front lines collides with enduring ties to Russia, personal convictions, and the everyday need to survive.” The Big Boom! premieres at IDFA on Saturday. articles.title: ‘NAZA’ Becomes One Of The Most Watched Docs On Theatrical Release In 2026
articles.content: Bombshell Gaza documentary NAZA by Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor is on track to become one of the most-watched documentary films on theatrical release of 2026. New figures, collated by producers The Guardian and JW Films, reveal that the film had been seen by a world-wide audience of 1,547,033 across 47 territories by November 6. With $13.5 million in international gross, excluding the U.S. where it has grossed more than $1 million, it ranks among the best-performing documentaries internationally of 2026 to date. Related Stories News Avi Nesher's Israeli Box Office Hit 'Our Loves' Brings Its Characters "To The Brink" But Is Not An "October 7 Movie" News Asian World Film Festival Reveals Asian Vision & Focus On Sections Based on interviews with 24 Israeli intelligence officers and soldiers, the documentary exposes the AI, phone surveillance and points-based systems deployed by the Israeli military in Gaza to identify targets, Hamas-related or otherwise, and then kill them in their homes regardless of whether other family members are likely to die in the strike as well. Watch on Deadline The documentary has performed best in Italy, where it was released by I Wonder on September 29 shortly after its Venice world premiere. The doc has reached 717.517 admissions there to date, with the film still playing in 379 cinemas, making history as the third most-watched documentary of all time in Italian cinemas, behind only Fahrenheit 9/11 and The March of the Penguins . Having started as a self-release through Michael Tuckman’s mTuckman Media in the U.S., Neon signed on as U.S. distributor in late October, aiming to enlarge the film’s footprint by building on the successful initial theatrical launch. To date the doc has clocked 83,673 admissions across the U.S. and Canada since its release on September 30. articles.title: ‘VisionQuest’ Teases Surprise ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Character Return In Post-Credits Scene
articles.content: SPOILERS: This post contains details about the VisionQuest Season 1 finale episode “Forever” A major player appears to be returning to the MCU following the Season 1 finale of VisionQuest . In a post-credits scene from Tuesday’s finale episode “Forever”, a hooded figure that appears to be Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom raises the rubble of Wundagore off Wanda Maximoff/Scarlet Witch ( Elizabeth Olsen ) after she seemingly killed herself under the collapsing mountain in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022). “Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine,” says the hooded figure. Watch on Deadline The post-credits scene seems to hint at Olsen’s return for Avengers: Doomsday , premiering Dec. 18 in theaters, after Vision (Paul Bettany) was reunited with both their sons, Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica) and Billy (Joe Locke), in the finale, which follows the events of WandaVision (2021) and Agatha All Along (2024). Marvel Studios hinted at the family potentially being fully reunited on social media ahead of Thursday’s finale, sharing a message in binary code that appears to translate to: “We could never truly leave each other, even if we tried.” Wanda previously said that to Tommy and Billy in the finale of WandaVision . Meanwhile, Olsen has said “ I know nothing ” when asked about her character’s potential return to the MCU. “I don’t know what’s going on. It’s safer for me to not know anything because then I can’t make a mistake in a situation like this. I rather know nothing,” she said in March.

articles.title: Amanda Seyfried Says ‘You Can See Everything’ Role “Scares” Her, “Feels Good” Taking On Doc
articles.content: While reprising one of her most talked about roles, Amanda Seyfried conquered some artistic fears. The You Can See Everything star, who appears in the A24 doc after her Emmy and Golden Globe-winning performance as its subject Elizabeth Holmes in Hulu’s The Dropout (2022), recently said she’s “relieved” and “excited” that her role in the Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim experimental film has been revealed. “It’s important for me as an actor, an artist, I mean, a mom, of course, but as a person in the world who loves to work, to find things that I haven’t done before and to do things that scare me in a specific way,” she told People . Seyfried added, “And when you follow through with something that scares you and it comes out the other end that it’s something that’s having an impact, mostly positive impact, it always feels good because you take a risk.” Watch on Deadline In You Can See Everything , disgraced Theranos founder invites Fielder into her and husband Billy Evans’ home to document everything in the month leading up to the start of her 11-year prison sentence on fraud charges. In a big twist, the documentary continues after Holmes reports to prison in Bryan, Texas in 2023, with Seyfried reprising her role in reenactments of moments that were not captured on video. With Seyfried’s appearance revealed during the doc’s surprise September premiere at Telluride, A24 has been building Oscar buzz for the actress, which would be the first time a documentary re-enactor has been nominated in an acting category.

articles.title: Stacy Keach Dies: ‘Mike Hammer’ Star, Film & Stage Actor Was 85
articles.content: Stacy Keach , the prolific actor who starred on TV’s Mike Hammer and Titus and recurred on Blue Bloods after establishing himself as a stage and film actor, died Monday. He was 85. His wife, Małgosia Tomassi, said he died “after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure” at the family home in Magdalenka, Poland. “Stacy was not only a legendary actor, admired and loved by audiences the world over, but also my beloved husband, my companion and the heart of our family,” she wrote. “His passing leaves an immeasurable emptiness in our lives. But his extraordinary spirit, his unforgettable voice and the love he gave so generously will remain with us forever.” Keach appeared in several Broadway, Off Broadway and local shows during the 1960s, often in Shakespeare plays, and earned a Best Actor Tony nomination and Drama Desk Award for playing Buffalo Bill in the 1970 play Indians. He would be inducted into the Theater Hall of Fame in 2015. He began landing film roles late in that decade. He starred as an aging, alcoholic boxer who works with a younger fighter (Jeff Bridges) in John Huston’s Fat City (1972) and played famed gunfighter Doc Holliday opposite Faye Dunaway in Doc (1971) and starred with George C. Scott in cop drama The New Centurians (1971). Other early film credits include The Life and Times of Judge Roy Bean (1972) with titular star Paul Newman; starring as Martin Luther in Luther (1974) and playing aviation pioneer Wilbur Wright in Orville and Wilbur (1972). Keach also began working in television during the 1960s, playing Banquo in a 1968 production of Macbeth and other telefilms. He also played Napoleon Bonaparte in The Man of Destiny (1973). His first series-regular role was starring as a police lieutenant in the one-season ABC drama Caribe in 1975. articles.title: Oscar Winner David Dinerstein Boards ‘Room Of The Absolute’ As EP; Award-Winning Doc Creates Portrait Of Ukrainian Artist Alla Hurenko
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Academy Award winner David Dinerstein has signed on to executive produce Room of the Absolute as the award-winning short documentary ramps up its Oscar campaign. The film directed by Natalie Shirinian and Elizabeth Baudouin fashions “an intimate, diaristic portrait of Ukrainian painter Alla Hurenko , professionally known as Pazza Pennello, who documented three years of her daily life under war entirely on an iPhone 14 while being directed remotely by her friends Shirinian and Baudouin from the United States.” PGA-nominated producer Christine Beebe ( Hal , Felix Austria! ) has also joined Room of the Absolute as executive producer. The film has won recognition at the Provincetown International Film Festival and the Minneapolis-St. Paul International Film Festival and earned Best Documentary Short nominations at the Woodstock and Mill Valley film festivals. articles.title: Doc Talk Podcast: Director Pegah Ahangarani On Her Oscar-Contending ‘Rehearsals For A Revolution’ And Trump’s Fateful Attack On Iran
articles.content: Filmmaker Pegah Ahangarani ’s journey to make the award-winning documentary Rehearsals for a Revolution began with the discovery of a photograph. She was visiting her grandmother’s house in Iran when she came upon an image. In the photo, “I noticed a man who was standing next to my father, but his face had been scratched out. I asked my grandmother, ‘Who is this person? Why his face has been scratched out?’” Ahangarani recalls. “She said, ‘He was your father’s best friend. And he was executed after the Revolution because he was a political prisoner.’” That disturbing story speaks to an experience common in the director’s family and in Iran as a whole – hopes raised by revolutionary fervor that end in terrible repression. Watch on Deadline Rehearsals for a Revolution premiered in Cannes where it won the l’Oeil d’or prize for the festival’s top documentary. It has also claimed best documentary wins at the Woodstock Film Festival in New York and the Montclair Film Festival in New Jersey, among other honors. It recently made the IDA Documentary Awards shortlist of the year’s best nonfiction features and was named to the Winners Circle at DOC NYC. It has since become the UK’s submission into the 2027 International Feature Film Oscar race . Ahangarani joins the latest edition of Deadline’s Doc Talk podcast to discuss her work on the deeply personal film that explores what her father, who initially supported the Islamic Revolution of 1979; her uncle, a beloved teacher; and others close to her went through as the theocratic regime asserted total control over its people. She says she sees her mission as making sure the faces scratched out of Iran’s history are not forgotten. The director also explores how the documentary reached its final form after three years of intense editing (a surprise guest drops by to reveal why Ahangarani often called him in middle of the night to scrap versions of the edit and start all over again). articles.title: Netflix Heads Back To The Jungle After Renewing Survival Competition Series ‘Outlast’
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE : The first two seasons of Netflix ’s survival competition series Outlast were set in the remote wilderness of Alaska. Earlier this year, season three took a new set of contestants to the Panamanian jungle and season four of the show will also take place in a dense forest. Netflix renewed the show, which comes from BBC Studios and Jason Bateman’s Aggregate Films, for a fourth season, which is also considered season two of Outlast: The Jungle . It will see 16 strangers put their survival skills to the test navigating scarce resources, brutal conditions, and alliances that shift without warning in order to outlast the rest and claim a $1M prize. It comes after Outlast: The Jungle premiered in June. The first six episodes launched on June 10 with the two-part finale dropping on June 17. [ SPOILER ALERT ] Team Alpha, consisting of Maddy Jones, a photographer from West Virginia, and Nikki Hru, a Florida-born boxer, won the prize after surviving a grueling two-day hike into the Panamanian jungle. Watch on Deadline This was in contrast with the first two seasons of the show, which were filmed in Chichagof Island, west of Juneau, and Little Duncan Bay, southwest of Petersburg, in Alaska. It’s not clear where season four will exactly take place but sources suggest it will move from Panama. Showrunner Mike Odair said season three “felt like throwing gasoline on the format”. “We traded the frozen isolation of Alaska for the heat and volatility of Panama, and everything changed: the survival, the strategy, and the social dynamics … This may be our most dynamic group yet,” he said ahead of the launch. Odair exec produces alongside Bateman and Michael Costigan and Emma Ho for Aggregate Films and Ryan O’Dowd and Krystal Whitney for BBC Studios.

articles.title: ITV Cutting $40M From Media & Entertainment Budget Due To Weak Advertising Market
articles.content: With “weaker demand for advertising” in Q4, ITV has identified £30M ($40M) worth of cost savings from its networks division, which will soon be sold to Sky . Total Advertising Revenue is set to drop 5-10% in Q4 and 2-3% for full year 2026, ITV said today in its Q3 trading update. articles.title: ITV’s Sale to Sky ‘Progressing as Planned’ as Broadcaster Cuts Fourth-Quarter Content Spend Amid U.K. Ad Slump
articles.content: U.K. broadcaster ITV ‘s CEO Carolyn McCall said the broadcaster’s sale of its Media & Entertainment business to Sky is “progressing as planned,” even as weaker advertiser demand forced the U.K. company to cut £25 million ($33.4 million) from its fourth-quarter content spend. The deal, which covers ITV’s channels and its ITVX streamer, would leave the company as a standalone global content group built around ITV Studios, the producer of “ The Gentlemen ” and “Line of Duty.” Comcast-owned Sky agreed in July to pay £1.6 billion ($2.1 billion) for the business, and ITV still expects it to close in the second half of 2027. On Nov. 4, U.K. Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy issued a Public Interest Intervention Notice on the takeover, as Variety reported , opening the way for the Competition and Markets Authority and media regulator Ofcom to examine it and report back to her. The business ITV is selling is also the one under pressure. The company now expects total advertising revenue to drop by around 5%–10% in the last three months of 2026 and by roughly 2%–3% across the full year, compared with 2025. ITV will also hold back £5 million ($6.7 million) of discretionary spending outside programming, so the temporary fourth-quarter cuts in Media & Entertainment add up to £30 million ($40 million). Its total 2026 content budget is now projected at about £1.2 billion ($1.6 billion). ITV blamed the slowdown on ongoing economic uncertainty, ad money moving toward global streamers and the U.K.’s restrictions on advertising for less healthy food, which kicked in on Oct. 1, 2025. articles.summary: He was a memorable Mike Hammer, starred in 'Fat City,' 'The New Centurions' and in Cheech & Chong films and excelled at Shakespeare on the stage.

He was 85. articles.title: ‘Long Long Night’ Director Youm Kyu-bock on Creating Animation That Takes Kids Seriously
articles.summary: The Korean filmmaker discusses the existential themes, environmental concerns and visual ambitions behind his acclaimed and unconventional animated feature debut.
articles.content: The Korean filmmaker discusses the existential themes, environmental concerns and visual ambitions behind his acclaimed and unconventional animated feature debut. Long Long Night is the rare children’s animation that respects its audience enough to believe they are equipped to handle some of the hardest realities of adult life — the inevitability of loneliness and the loss of our dearest loved ones, not to mention the cold, uncaring nature of the cosmos. The film is also beautifully poignant in its depiction of how we can create meaning and forge loving connections despite the fundamental brutality of our existential plight. Not bad for a colorful road movie for kids featuring a gentle rhinoceros and a baby penguin. The film marks the feature debut of Korean filmmaker Youm Kyu-bock, who spent two decades directing commercials, including campaigns for Samsung, BMW and Canon. A visual design graduate of Kookmin University, Youm worked as a producer at AlphaVille 44 and a director at Elvis Production before becoming CEO of GoogGoog Studio, an advertising and branded-content company now venturing into original features. Independent animated features remain relatively uncommon in South Korea, and the production tested how far Youm could stretch a budget of about 5 billion won ($3.7 million). He estimates that the film took four-and-a-half years to make, including an 18-month pause when funding ran short. The animation team typically numbered about 60, rising to roughly 120 artists at the height of production. Youm’s film is adapted from an award-winning children’s book of the same name that has sold more than 800,000 copies in South Korea. The story’s hero, Norden, is a White Boulder rhino who experiences the uniquely tragic plight of becoming the last living example of his species (the book’s author, Ru Ri, took inspiration from Sudan, the real-life last male northern white rhinoceros who died in captivity in 2018). articles.content: JoBe Cerny, who voiced the playful Pillsbury Doughboy in commercials and appeared in films including Somewhere in Time , My Best Friend’s Wedding and Road to Perdition , has died. He was 78. Cerny lived in Grayslake, Illinois, and died Oct. 30, his family announced . He had battled Alzheimer’s disease. For more than 30 years, Cerny owned and operated Cerny/American Creative Recording Studio in the River North neighborhood of Chicago. His company completed thousands of projects, including commercials, features and audiobooks. Related Stories Movies Stacy Keach, Who Played Badasses With the Best of Them, Dies at 85 TV Toukie Smith, Top Runway Model and '227' Actress, Dies at 74 One of his finest accomplishments was directing a 98-hour dramatized audio production of the New King James Version of the Bible called The Word of Promise that featured more than 500 actors, among them Jim Caviezel as Jesus, Marisa Tomei as Mary Magdalene, Richard Dreyfuss as Moses, Gary Sinise as David, Jason Alexander as Joseph, Max von Sydow as Noah, Jon Voight as Abraham, Luke Perry as Judas and Marcia Gay Harden as Esther. Cerny also converted episodes of CBS’ The Twilight Zone into radio programing and wrote new installments for a podcast series. Cerny succeeded Paul Frees and Jeff Bergman as the high-pitched voice of the Pillsbury Co.’s cheerful Pillsbury Doughboy , who giggled when poked in the belly (he played the lovable Poppin’ Fresh character until about 2020). “I’ve gone through phases over the years,” he said in a 2007 interview . “Sometimes [Pillsbury gets] a new executive. articles.title: A Decade After ‘Parks and Rec,’ Amy Poehler Is Back on TV With ‘Dig’: “I Was Waiting for the Right Thing”
articles.summary: Poehler has re-teamed with 'Parks and Rec' creator Mike Schur for the new series, which follows a group of archaeologists on a dig in Greece.
articles.content: Amy Poehler may have a new career as a podcasting mogul , with her show Good Hang , but the comedy star is going back to her TV roots. Poehler has re-teamed with Parks and Recreation creator Mike Schur for new series Dig , which follows a group of archaeologists (and some college students) who spend their summer working on a dig site in Greece. When they discover a rare artifact that could change history, they become entangled in a dangerous international conspiracy. Poehler is joined on the cast by Hugh Laurie, Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas and Fina Strazza, and came to Schur with the idea to adapt Kate Myers’ bestselling novel Excavations as a series. articles.title: Casey Bloys Tapped for Producers Guild Milestone Award
articles.summary: The Skydance direct-to-consumer co-chair and HBO head joins a list of recent recipients that includes Jason Blum and Dana Walden.
articles.content: The Producers Guild of America has named Casey Bloys the recipient of its Milestone Award for 2027. Bloys, co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance Direct-to-Consumer, will receive the honor at the guild’s 38th annual awards on Feb. 27. The Milestone Award honors people or teams who have made “historic contributions” to the industry. “Considering Hollywood’s recent history, no one is more deserving of the Milestone Award than Casey Bloys, PGA presidents Donna Gigliotti and Mike Farah said in a statement. “Over the last decade, Casey has had a front row seat to all the disruption and consolidation facing our industry. All the while he has remained a true and steadfast champion of the creative process. He is a friend to producers, writers, actors and everyone who has dedicated their lives and careers to entertainment. Casey and his talented team help shepherd television that shapes our culture, stands the test of time, and protects the originality of storytellers. While Casey is never one to seek the spotlight, the Producers Guild of America is proud to recognize the breadth and depth of his exceptional career with the Milestone Award.” Related Stories Business Webby Awards Launches IMDB-Like Credits Platform to Provide Verified Recognition for Creators Amid AI Growth (Exclusive) Movies Ridley Scott Will Miss Academy's Governors Awards, Accept Honorary Oscar Remotely (Exclusive) Bloys became head of HBO in 2016. In the past decade, HBO and HBO Max have debuted series including Succession, Big Little Lies, Euphoria, Insecure, The White Lotus, The Last of Us and a number of other Emmy-winning and critically acclaimed shows. articles.title: CBS Unveils Competitors for Drew Barrymore-Hosted ‘Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic’ Special (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Famed baker and author Amirah Kassem will join Barrymore and celebrity chef judges Christina Tosi and Dook Chase in the Nov. 23 special.
articles.content: Twenty-four home bakers are joining CBS ‘ Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic special, hosted by Drew Barrymore . In addition, famed baker and author Amirah Kassem has come on board as a roaming sideline reporter, bringing viewers real-time reactions from the bakers, their families and the audience. The show also features celebrity chef judges Christina Tosi and Dook Chase. The 24 contestants will be divided into four groups of six, with each group competing in its own head-to-head round themed around an iconic holiday staple: cookies, cakes, pies or biscuits. The top baker from each round will advance to the “Best in Bake” finale, where they will create “Edible Festive Wreaths for the Holidays.” Related Stories TV 'Survivor 51' Castoff Brady Booker on That "Toxicity" Comment, Starving Through Challenges and What It Means to Be a "Brodie" General News Trump Reflects on Republicans' Midterm Losses, Reacts to J.D. Vance's Own Analysis in '60 Minutes' Interview The winner will be crowned the 2026 Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic c hampion, which comes with a $25,000 cash prize, a complete KitchenAid equipment package and the Pillsbury Golden Rolling Pin trophy. In total, there have been 53 previous Pillsbury Bake-Off competitions, dating back to 1949. The special will air Nov. 23 from 8-10 p.m. ET/PT on CBS and stream on Paramount+ (Premium). Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic is produced by Studio Large Eyes, Pantheon Media Group and Juma Entertainment. Executive producers include Scott Weintrob for Studio Large Eyes, Jennifer O’Connell, Ariel Brozell, Eden Sutley and Martha Chaput for Pantheon, Robert Horowitz for Juma Entertainment and Brielle Cohen is showrunner. Lisa Balzo, Kenzie Caron and Eleanor Harkness serve as executive producers for Pillsbury.

articles.title: BBC Studios Names Sreya Biswas New Head of Its Natural History Unit
articles.summary: Reporting to Kate Ward, managing director, unscripted at BBC Studios, she will work alongside creative directors Mike Gunton and Jonny Keeling.
articles.content: BBC Studios has named Sreya Biswas the new head of its Natural History Unit (NHU). She takes over from Jonny Keeling, who is moving into a new role from early 2027, as previously unveiled. Reporting to Kate Ward , managing director, unscripted at BBC Studios , Biswas will work alongside creative directors Keeling and Mike Gunton, overseeing the unit’s teams based in Bristol. “Biswas will lead the editorial, commercial and strategic direction for the NHU as it sets an ambitious growth strategy for the future,” the company said. Biswas joined BBC Studios in the summer 2025 as the NHU’s Director of programs, where she oversaw a number of commissioned titles and the development of a portfolio of new content for multiple global clients across platforms, including the first BBC visualized nature podcast Naturewatch, feature documentary Matriarch , and Blue Planet III . Previously, she was served as head of commissioning for Natural History at the BBC, where she oversaw some of the landmark TV series, including Planet Earth III, Asia, Kingdom and Blue Planet III , as well as commissioning a broad range of natural history content, including Big Cats 24/7, Hamza’s Hidden Wild Isles, Spy in the Troop and A n Hour on Earth . Biswas also oversaw feature documentaries, such as Silverback and Orphan , as well as environmental thriller On Thin Ice: Putin v Greenpeace . “Sreya marries her extraordinary creative reputation and deep passion for the people and programmes of the NHU, with a razor-sharp future-facing vision that will look to deepen and strength how audiences can connect to the stories of the natural world,” said Ward. “We are delighted to welcome her to this pivotal role and look forward to continued success for the NHU under her inspiring leadership.” Said Biswas: “I feel hugely privileged to be stepping into this role, working alongside Mike Gunton and Jonny Keeling and leading the NHU’s remarkable teams. articles.title: Olivia Cooke Says ‘House of the Dragon’ Fandom Led to Her Social Media Break: “A Lot of Ugliness”
articles.summary: The actress plays the controversial Queen Alicent Hightower in HBO’s 'Game of Thrones' prequel series.
articles.content: Olivia Cooke is getting candid about one of the reasons she took a break from social media, saying there’s “a lot of ugliness” in House of the Dragon fandom. The actress, who plays controversial Queen Alicent Hightower in HBO’s Game of Thrones prequel series, recently chatted with GQ about the passionate yet intense fanbase that often theorizes about not only her character but sometimes herself and her relationship with directors. “I think some of those interpretations just catch fire, and they become something that bears no resemblance to what was shown on the screen at the time,” Cooke said. “There’s a lot of ugliness to that fandom as well. It’s steeped in misogyny. There’s a lot of racism. I try to let it take up minimal mental real estate.” Related Stories Movies 'Long Long Night' Director Youm Kyu-bock on Creating Animation That Takes Kids Seriously Movies Brandon Sklenar on 'Iron Jane,' Body Dysmorphia and His Rapid Hollywood Rise Eventually, the fan discourse on social media reached a point that was “not nourishing” for the actress, which is partly why she deactivated her social media accounts ahead of the House of the Dragon season three premiere in June. “I was just like, I’m on this too much. It’s not nourishing,” she said. “I think the celebri-fied nature of being an actor has now snowballed into this monster. And I just think we need to get off this train and realise that we make these TV shows and films, yes, for escapism, but also because it’s artful and it’s creative and it’s not for followers or for a brand deal or to get free shit. articles.title: ‘The Other Elliot Sister’ Greenlit at BritBox With Launch of Austen Anthology Franchise (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Elizabeth Elliot of 'Persuasion' will receive 'The Other Bennet Sister' treatment in a 10-part series as Mary Bennet's record-breaking popularity spawns an entire franchise dedicated to Jane Austen's forgotten heroines.
articles.content: All of Jane Austen ‘s wallflowers will be given their chance to bloom as BritBox launches an anthology franchise off the back of The Other Bennet Sister ‘s success. The BBC Studios-owned streamer has unveiled to The Hollywood Reporter a series titled Austen Untold , made in partnership with The Other Bennet Sister ‘s production company Bad Wolf , dedicated to TV show adaptations of Austen stories told through the perspectives of overlooked and under-explored characters. The Other Elliot Sister , following the eldest sibling of Austen’s Persuasion , has been commissioned to mark Austen Untold ‘s launch. The 10-part drama is adapted by The Other Bennet Sister writer Sarah Quintrell from Janice Hadlow’s forthcoming novel of the same name. With production set to kick off in 2027, the show will build on the approach established by the much-loved Other Bennet Sister by placing a character previously confined to the margins at the heart of her own story. articles.title: Coachella 2027 Sets Dua Lipa, Tame Impala, SZA and Daddy Yankee as Headliners
articles.summary: Madonna, Zara Larsson, Weezer and Kehlani are also among the performers The post Coachella 2027 Sets Dua Lipa, Tame Impala, SZA and Daddy Yankee as Headliners appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala, SZA and Daddy Yankee have been locked in to headline the 2027 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, the event’s organizers shared on Tuesday. Passes for the event will go on sale on Friday at 12 p.m. PT. However, AMEX Presale Passes will go on sale a day earlier on Thursday at 12 p.m. PT. The two-weekend event is set for Friday, April 9 through Sunday, April 11, and again on Friday, April 16 through Sunday, April 18. Daddy Yankee has been selected as a fourth headliner and is slated to perform in a special production. YouTube once again returns as the event’s official streaming partner. In addition to the aforementioned headliners, other notable performers set for the festival include Madonna, Zara Larsson, Steve Lacey, JISOO, Kehlani, Leon Thomas, Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, Tiësto, Martin Garrix, Role Model, Adéla, Don Toliver, Dom Dolla, Kygo, The Neighbourhood and Becky G. The 2027 headliners follow a star-studded 2026 lineup, which saw Justin Bieber, Sabrina Carpenter, Karol G and Anyma lead the music-filled weekend. Carpenter, especially, made a splash with her numerous celebrity cameos – including Susan Sarandon, Will Ferrell, Corey Fogelmanis, Geena Davis, Terry Crews and Madonna – in a theatrical production staging her latest hits. As for Bieber, while Coachella marked his big return to performing, the music sensation faced criticism for his sparse set and low-effort performance while singing along to older tracks.

articles.content: Showrunner Terry Matalas tells TheWrap his thinking on the Scarlet Witch for this Marvel show “VisionQuest” wrapped up its run on Tuesday night, thus ending the Disney+ trilogy that began back in 2021 with “WandaVision.” The big question is: Did that finale bring the return of Elizabeth Olsen as Wanda Maximoff? “Agatha All Along,” the second show in the trilogy between “WandaVision” and “VisionQuest” played jump rope with whether Wanda was really dead, leaving many to hope she might return to reunite with her family in this series. With the appearance of — here’s your last spoiler warning! — Joe Locke’s Billy Maximoff in the finale, that hope only grew stronger. Alas, no, Wanda Maximoff didn’t return as well — at least, not in the actual “VisionQuest” story arc. But, according to showrunner Terry Matalas, the idea of bringing the witch back for this family reunion was on the table. “Listen, the Wanda conversation was constant, and if we felt strong enough about it, we would have done it,” he explained to TheWrap. “But the second it — and there were pages written of an element of things. There’s a couple of them, but it always consumed the story in a way that detracted from Vision’s in a way.” “When you introduce Wanda again, it needs to be her story, instead of her coming in and out of this other thing,” he continued. “So that’ll be up to the Marvel gods as to what happens with that. But you know, stay tuned.” Fans didn’t have to stay tuned for very long, as “VisionQuest” did include an unexpected Wanda scene (one that was not included in the episode screener sent to press). First, we re-live Wanda collapsing the temple of the Scarlet Witch on herself, which is painful. But suddenly, Doctor Doom appears. Sure enough, Elizabeth Olsen is in the rubble and her eyes shoot open. So, it would appear that fan theories are correct, and the Scarlet Witch will return in “Avengers: Doomsday.”

articles.content: The charges against Amazon’s epic (and epically priced) “Lord of the Rings” series, “The Rings of Power,” stacked up quickly. The first two seasons were pretty good by blockbuster standards — and I wasn’t alone in saying so — but the record-breaking costs, as well as the franchise’s lofty pedigree, set expectations higher than Great Eagles can soar. Tolkien’s text — at least, not on at any depth . Mayer, Walt Disney, Alfred Hitchcock, Steven Spielberg, Sherry Lansing, James Cameron, Bob Iger, Donna Langley, Ted Sarandos, George Lucas and Kathleen Kennedy, Charles D. King, Dana Walden, and Jason Blum. articles.title: ‘Victorian Psycho’ Review: Maika Monroe Scares Up a Very Different Kind of Final Girl
articles.summary: In Zachary Wigon’s deliciously dark adaptation of Virginia Feito's novel of the same name, the beloved scream queen switches sides. Kind of.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on May 21, 2026 during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. Bleecker Street will release the film in theaters Friday, November 13.] Winifred Notty is the sanest person she knows, or so the heroine (or anti-heroine, depending on how you might see it) of Zachary Wigon’s “Victorian Psycho” is quick to tell anyone who will listen. Or not, as star Maika Monroe delivers that damning and darkly funny insight into Winifred’s soul via a prim voiceover that seems to exist for her own benefit as much as the audience she seems to imagine. That’s tangled enough, but there’s also this: Winifred doesn’t really know that many people, mostly because just about everyone she’s come across in her life is dead. Still, sane! Ish. Well, it’s not called “ Victorian Psycho ” for nothing. Related Stories ‘Steps’ Review: A Disposable Fairy Tale Reminds Us That Cinderella Is Someone’s Hated Stepsister Too ‘The Debut’ Trailer: Julianne Moore Goes Full Julianne Moore in Jesse Eisenberg’s Riotously Funny Musical Theater Comedy Adapted for the screen by novelist Virginia Feito from her own work, the book comes recommended alongside its predecessor, “Mrs. March,” for anyone drawn to entertainment with “psycho” in the title. articles.title: ‘Steps’ Review: A Disposable Fairy Tale Reminds Us That Cinderella Is Someone’s Hated Stepsister Too
articles.summary: Reimagining fairy tales from other characters' perspectives no longer wins you points for originality, but Netflix's latest animation effort might entertain children who aren't old enough to be bored by the formula.
articles.content: The so-called villains of our childhood stories aren’t so bad when you look at things from their points of view. It’s a lesson that 21st century pop culture has taught us on a constant loop ever since “Wicked” kicked off an Oppenheimer-esque chain of tragedy that has seen everyone from Maleficent to Cruella de Vil humanized with their own origin story. It was inevitable that Cinderella’s allegedly wicked stepsisters would get their own mainstream version of the formula at some point (the Norwegian body horror movie exists in a separate, more ambitious category). If Hollywood can try to make us emphasize with someone who lives to kill puppies, anyone could have guessed that someone would slap a generational trauma label on literal children who grew up under the same evil matriarch as Cinderella. articles.summary: James Graham adapts his own hit West End and Broadway play into a Netflix Oscar hopeful.
articles.content: If you like your media industry dramas to be based in reality but still can’t resist a salacious power struggle, “Ink” might be the movie for you this holiday season. Danny Boyle ‘s Netflix thriller dramatizes the beginnings of Rupert Murdoch’s empire, following the future mogul when he was just a young Australian newspaper man. When he launched The Sun alongside former business partner Larry Lamb in 1969, the two men effectively created the modern tabloid and figured out that audiences were hungry for a lot more than just truth. Their sensationalist approach to journalism would come in handy on many of Murdoch’s future business endeavors, and the film draws a very clear line between his editorial preferences and the 2026 world he helped create for us.
